title: Squat: Quant Small Language Models on the Edge
problem: Small language models on edge devices are memory- and compute-bound; aggressive quantization enables deployment but risks accuracy loss without careful method design.
motivation: Efficient SLM inference on edge devices is critical for privacy-preserving and low-latency AI applications; quantization without quality degradation unlocks resource-constrained deployment.
method: The approach reduces number precision in small language models using low-bit formats (INT8 and INT4—8 or 4 bits per number instead of 32) and tailors this reduction to the model's architecture. It implements this on edge CPUs and microcontrollers using code optimized for SIMD (a CPU feature that processes many numbers in parallel). To maintain accuracy despite this aggressive shrinking, it uses knowledge distillation (training the small model with guidance from a larger one) and activation-aware quantization (cutting precision more aggressively in less-important computational parts). This combination keeps the models accurate while fitting them onto memory-limited edge devices.
key_novelty: The core innovation is a complete quantization system that reduces small language models to run on SIMD-capable edge processors while maintaining accuracy.
contributions: SLM-optimized quantization methodology for edge devices
SIMD kernel optimization for quantized inference
Knowledge distillation integration for quality maintenance
limitations: Analysis limited to title and abstract; specific edge device targets and accuracy benchmarks not detailed.
primary_theme: quantized SLM inference on SIMD edge devices
